1. Introduction                                                        exhibit impressive capabilities in robotic scene understand-

language models [1, 33], vision-language-action (VLA)                  tion and manipulation performance in out-of-lab scenar-
models have emerged [9, 36] and are trained on robot                   ios [5, 27, 48]. Such advances have significantly acceler-

Figure 2. Framework of ManualVLA. (a) To accomplish long-horizon tasks with defined goal states, we propose ManualVLA, a unified
VLA model built upon a MoT architecture. The framework consists of two experts: a planning expert responsible for generating multimodal
manuals, and an action expert responsible for predicting precise actions. The planning expert processes human instructions, the current
image, and the final goal image to generate intermediate manuals that combine next-step images, positions, and sub-task instructions. We
introduce an explicit CoT reasoning process, where each positional indicator serves as a visual prompt embedded into the observation of the
action expert. (b) Along with the cross-task shared attention mechanism and the designed attention mask, the generated manual tokens are
also used as conditioning signals for action generation, enabling an implicit CoT reasoning process that effectively guides the action expert.
(c) ManualVLA adopts a three-stage training strategy that aligns the planning and action experts for effective collaboration.

tasks while preserving its ability to learn cross-task depen-                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      weight matrix A is computed globally across all tokens. 3.5. Real-to-Render Data Generation                                                       We compare ManualVLA against three categories of strong
